slot_note: seed ET34 (QCEW county wage jump): the world, the decision and the quantity kept (a county's private pay per job and which industries' pay really grew); the pitfall re-found from the record's own calendar structure
niche: a regional workforce board conforming its county's quarterly covered-wage record (wages counted in the quarter they are paid) to pay for the work done in each calendar year, to rank industries' 2021 to 2025 pay growth per job for its 2027 sector-partnership slate
answer: Name Information, Finance and insurance, Professional, scientific, and technical services, and Construction as the 2027 to 2029 sector-partnership slate; Manufacturing is next in line.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the county file's three releases, reads that wages are counted in the quarter they are paid and every rule correctly, and ranks wages per job as recorded, or corrects with one assumed pay-schedule mix or with Friday pay dates (normal in both 2021 and 2025), files Information, Finance and insurance, Transportation and warehousing and Health care on the slate, because 2025 carried an extra Thursday pay date (New Year's Day 2026 paid on 31 December 2025) for the share of each industry's payroll run on Thursdays, recorded nowhere and largest in hospitals and trucking and warehousing.
domain_test: The decisive quantity is each industry's growth in pay per job for the work done in 2021 and 2025, which needs each industry's calendar (pay-date) effect estimated the way official time-series production estimates calendar regressors: from how its quarterly wages per job move with the Friday and Thursday pay dates of each alternate-week phase each quarter holds over thirteen years; swapping in another field's nouns breaks it because the pay-date calendar, the holiday rule that moves a pay date across the year end, the quarter-of-payment rule of unemployment-insurance wage reporting and the mix of payroll schedules are what create and identify the effect.

spine.entity: one county, ownership and industry code in one quarter

world.geography: United States, a fictional multi-county labor market region (unnamed state)

driver: A periodic total is recorded in the period each payment is made, payments recur on fixed-interval schedules on different weekdays and phases, and a payment date falling on a holiday moves to the day before, so in some periods one weekday's schedules carry an extra payment while other weekdays' do not; each unit's exposure to every schedule is recorded nowhere and is estimated from how its recorded sub-period totals move with the payment dates each sub-period holds, before growth between two periods is measured on the work done.
driver_concrete: 2025 holds a 53rd Thursday and a 27th pay date for one alternate-Thursday phase (New Year's Day 2026 paid on 31 December 2025) while 2021 and every Friday schedule are normal, so each industry's exposure to every Friday and Thursday phase is estimated from how its quarterly wages per job since 2013 move with the pay dates each quarter holds, and its 2021 and 2025 wages are put on the work done before its 2021 to 2025 growth in pay per job is ranked for the slate.
stump: The default path ranks industries on 2021 to 2025 growth in covered wages per job as recorded, and a Friday-only payday check finds nothing to correct; both file Information, Finance and insurance, Transportation and warehousing and Health care, because 2025's extra Thursday pay date inflates the industries that pay largely on Thursdays; estimating each industry's exposure to every pay-date phase from its quarterly record files Information, Finance and insurance, Professional, scientific, and technical services and Construction.
